title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the list 'Quelques complexes d'algèbre différentielle' from p.218. A is a commutative ring, M an A-module, and Λ = Λ*M is the exterior algebra (Grothendieck writes Λ with a check or a dot over it). Page 218 gave (1) the de Rham differential on Sym*M⊗Λ*M and (2) the Koszul differential on Sym*M⊗Λ*M. This page gives their divided-power analogues.

(3) 'De Rham P.D.' On Γ*M⊗Λ*M there is a unique A-linear antiderivation d of degree 1 (in the Λ-degree) such that:
- d is compatible with the divided powers on Γ⁺M, i.e. d(x^{[i]}) = x^{[i-1]}dx;
- d vanishes on ΛM;
- on Γ¹M, d is the canonical isomorphism Γ¹M → Λ¹M.
Then d² = 0, d maps Γ^p⊗Λ^q to Γ^{p-1}⊗Λ^{q+1}, and d is ΛM-linear. This complex is the PD de Rham complex Ω_{Γ(M)/A,PD} of the PD algebra (Γ*M, Γ⁺M). For M flat, its cohomology is A in degree 0 (= Γ⁰⊗Λ⁰) and 0 elsewhere. This is the PD Poincaré lemma, and it holds with no characteristic assumption. It is proved by Künneth reduction to rank 1, then Lazard plus filtered colimits for flat M; the next page indicates exactly this argument.

(4) 'Koszul P.D.' On Γ*M⊗Λ*M there is a unique antiderivation δ that:
- vanishes on Γ¹M (hence, being Γ*M-linear, on all of Γ*M);
- is the canonical map Λ¹M → Γ¹M on Λ¹M.
It satisfies δ² = 0, maps Γ^p⊗Λ^q to Γ^{p+1}⊗Λ^{q-1}, and is Γ*M-linear. With homological indexing, for M flat and A of characteristic 0, the homology is A in degree 0. In characteristic p>0 he expects 'une histoire d'opérations de Cartier', as he said for (1) on the previous page.

The structure behind the four complexes:
- In rank 1, (1) is x^p ↦ p x^{p-1}dx and (4) is x^{[p]}⊗e ↦ (p+1)x^{[p+1]}. Both are exact only when integers are invertible, and in char p their (co)homology is Cartier-type, Frobenius-twisted.
- (2) and (3) are exact over any base.
- For M finite free, (1) and (4) are graded A-duals of each other (Γ(M^∨) = Sym(M)^∨), as are (2) and (3). This explains why the 'Cartier story' attaches precisely to (1) and (4).

The next page compares Sym→Γ and reduces the computation of (3) to rank 1 and that of (4) to (2). The purpose of the page is the 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex, i.e. the local algebra behind crystalline cohomology (Berthelot).
errors: In (4), condition b) ('compatible avec p.d. sur Γ⁺(M), d(x^{(i)}) = x^{(i-1)}dx') is copied from (3). It contradicts c) (δ vanishes on Γ¹M) and the stated Γ*M-linearity, under which δ(x^{[i]}) = 0. The correct defining data are: δ is Γ*M-linear and δ on Λ¹M is the canonical map to Γ¹M.
In (4), 'dérivation' should be 'antidérivation', as in the other three cases.
In (3), the cohomology statement is written with an unspecified index (H^•, then 'si i≠0'). The intended indexing is by Λ-degree; note that the complex also splits by total degree p+q.

Not stated explicitly: the characteristic-0 hypothesis is needed for (1) and (4) but not for (2) and (3), which hold over any base for flat M. Grothendieck's hypotheses on the page are consistent with this ('si M est plat' alone for (3); 'car. 0' for (4)).

ideas.what: PD de Rham complex of Γ_A(M) and the divided-power Poincaré lemma: Γ*M⊗Λ*M is a resolution of A for M flat, in all characteristics
ideas.modern_name: PD Poincaré lemma / divided-power de Rham complex
ideas.where_published: Ideas from Grothendieck's 1966 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (IHÉS notes, Dix exposés), developed by Berthelot; no explicit published statement by Grothendieck known

ideas.what: Divided-power Koszul complex Γ*M⊗Λ*M with Γ-linear δ, acyclic in characteristic 0
ideas.modern_name: Koszul complex with divided powers (dual Koszul complex)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Koszul; Illusie (Complexe cotangent I, Ch. I §4.3); Akin–Buchsbaum–Weyman

ideas.what: Characteristic-p homology of (1) and (4) governed by Cartier operations, with (1) and (4) graded-dual to each other
ideas.modern_name: Cartier isomorphism for the polynomial algebra and its dual; Frobenius twist

missed.claim: Grothendieck anticipates an explicit Cartier-type description of the homology of the PD Koszul complex in char p. Via duality with the de Rham complex of Sym, this is a dual Cartier isomorphism for Γ⊗Λ. It is known in substance (Illusie, and work on Koszul and Schur complexes in char p), so there is no real gap.
missed.quote: Si A de car. p>0, M plat, on doit avoir une histoire d'opération de Cartier...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It is a small instance of the Cartier/conjugate-filtration phenomena now treated systematically, e.g. derived de Rham cohomology and Bhatt's work, but it is not a missed result.

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard lecture-note lists of four classical complexes (de Rham and Koszul, with and without divided powers) with their acyclicity statements, all well known by 1976 (Berthelot, Illusie). The page is a clean organisation of known material, with one copy-paste inconsistency in (4).
transcription_corrections: The 'ΛM' written with dot/check/hat accents in the transcription is simply the exterior algebra Λ*M throughout; the accents are not distinct objects.
In (4), 'Excluant les degrés en bas si (limité)' is better read as 'Écrivant les degrés en bas, si M est plat sur A (libre?) et de car. 0, on a:', i.e. homological indexing.
In (4), the inserted phrase reads 'Alors δ²=0, il applique Γ^p⊗Λ^q dans Γ^{p+1}⊗Λ^{q-1}, et est Γ*M-linéaire', replacing a crossed-out fragment that starts 'A (est) ... alors δ²=0'.

In (3), the 'b)' insertion reads 'antidérivation de degré 1' over 'compatible avec les puiss. divisées sur (Γ*M)⁺'. Also, 'A-algèbre graduée' is inserted above the crossed-out 'Γ*(M) de degrés pairs'.
